exposure: feeding patterns (percentage of breast milk received, average daily formula consumption from birth to 6 months)
outcome: infant weight at 7-12 months of age (categorized as high or normal)
cohort: The study included 1799 mother-infant dyads enrolled in the Infant Feeding Practices Study II.
finding: A lower proportion of breast milk feedings from birth to 6 months was associated with excess weight at 7-12 months of age, particularly in high birth weight infants.
birth_weight: >=2500 g (classified as high >=4000g and normal >=2500g and <4000g)
gest_age: used for birth weight percentile adjustment
